on 8 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/70566970/
1
Court in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application u/s 438 Cr.P.C. No.387 of 2022 in Case Crime No. 201 of 2021, u/s 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B of IPC, Police Station - Bihar, District - Unnao.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that the O.P Nos. 2 to 4 were granted anticipatory bail by this Court vide order dated 27.07.2022 but they have flouted the condition no. 6 provided in the said order.

The order-sheet indicates that even the charge has not been framed as the O.P. Nos.
2 to 4 keep on evading the trial court proceedings by remaining absent and moving adjournment applications alternatively, as such, their anticipatory bail deserve to be cancelled.
5.

On the other hand, learned counsel for the O.P. Nos. 2 to 4 has argued that the O.P. Nos. 2 to 4 are cooperating with the trial and their discharge application was pending and the delay, if any,
could be attributed to the trial court only and not to them.
6. Anticipatory bail is intended to protect individuals against possible arrest, but it should not be used as a means to delay or obstruct the legal process.

Courts have repeatedly emphasized that while the provision safeguards an accused's liberty, it must not become a tool for misuse, such as deploying tactics that stall trial proceedings or hinder justice.
7. When anticipatory bail is granted, the accused is expected to fully cooperate with the investigation and the judicial process.
If the accused uses legal maneuvers (like repeated or unnecessary adjournments) to prolong the case and keep the trial from moving forward, courts may consider revoking bail.
This is especially pertinent when applications, such as for discharge, remain pending and the trial is at a standstill.

8. The Supreme Court and various High Courts have consistently held that bail provisions should not defeat the object of timely justice, and efforts to exploit procedural aspects to delay trial can result in adverse consequences for the accused, including cancellation of bail and expediting proceedings.

9. After hearing learned counsel for the parties and taking into consideration the fact that the O.P.
Nos. 2 to 4 are not cooperating with the trial as the charge has not been framed after passing of three year from the date the anticipatory bail granted, the present anticipatory bail cancellation application deserves to be allowed.
10. Accordingly, the present anticipatory bail cancellation application is allowed.

The order dated 27.07.2022 passed by this Court in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application u/s 438 Cr.P.C.
No.387 of 2022 in Case Crime No. 201 of 2021, u/s 420, 467, 468, 471, 120-B of IPC, Police Station - Bihar, District - Unnao, granting anticipatory bail to the O.P. Nos. 2 to 4, is hereby set aside.

11. However, four weeks' time from the date of pronouncement of this judgement is granted to the O.P. Nos. 2 to 4 to surrender before the trial court concerned and thereafter, it will be open for him to pray for regular bail, which may be considered in accordance with law.
